how: Every predicted signal of the 15 test compounds more than 3 ppm from NMRShiftDB2's measured shift, by compound and carbons (Molfile atom indices of tests/fixtures/nmr/<compound>.mol). Recorded so they are not hidden: web/scripts/nmr.test.ts fails if the predictions change. The values are in BUILD-LEARNINGS.md; 'why' is Claude's reading.

outliers.name: toluene
outliers.why: ipso carbon: toluene itself is left out of the table, and at 3 bonds the table mixes toluenes with any para substituent

outliers.name: p-cresol
outliers.why: the carbon bearing CH3; its only measured spectra are in DMSO-d6 and D2O, not CDCl3

outliers.name: benzaldehyde
outliers.why: para carbon: the C=O that deshields it is 5 bonds away, past the 4 the table describes

outliers.name: propanoic acid
outliers.why: COOH carbon: measured in CDCl3 (H-bonded dimer), while the table's acids are mostly in other solvents; matched at 2 bonds

outliers.name: 2-butanol
outliers.why: CH2: matched only at 2 bonds (low confidence)

outliers.name: aniline
outliers.why: para carbon: an NH2 and an amide's NH look alike to the code, and anilides dominate the table

outliers.name: triethylamine
outliers.why: CH2 next to N: few tertiary ethylamines like it in the table

outliers.name: cyclohexanamine
outliers.why: CH2 next to the CH-NH2: matched only at 2 bonds (low confidence)
